# Invariant

> Autonomous agents for the physical economy.

Read the full data, site selection, power and compliance guides at https://invariant-ai.com/llms-full.txt. Each guide and glossary entry has a Markdown copy at its URL plus `.md` (for example https://invariant-ai.com/blog/utility-grade-power-study.md).

Invariant builds autonomous agents for the physical economy. The agents connect design documents and test data to applicable regulations, then draft submissions, test plans, and compliance matrices with citations to the source requirements. Invariant serves teams in aerospace, energy, data centers, and oil and gas. Domain engineers handle deployment and review. Backed by Entrepreneur First, Transpose Platform, Boundless Ventures, and NPU Ventures.

## Key facts

- **State-of-the-art retrieval in nuclear:** Helion-512, our domain-adapted retrieval model, is the published state of the art on **FermiBench** (**0.9693 nDCG@10**), the only public retrieval benchmark for the nuclear regulatory domain.
- **Industries served:**
  - **Space:** FAA 14 CFR Part 450 (launch + reentry), FCC Part 25 (satellite communications), NOAA Commercial Space Licensing (Earth-observation data), IN-SPACe NGP 2024 (Indian space authorisations), ITU radio coordination, ECSS standards, NASA GEVS (GSFC-STD-7000), MIL-STD-1540, MIL-STD-461 (EMI/EMC).
  - **Aerospace:** FAA 14 CFR Part 21/23/25 (type certification, airworthiness) for crewed and unmanned aviation systems.
  - **Nuclear:** US NRC 10 CFR Parts 50, 52, 53, 100, 110; IAEA SSR-2/1; for advanced reactor and SMR developers, including Safety Analysis Report (PSAR / FSAR) authoring and Request-for-Additional-Information (RAI) handling.
- **Founded** 2025. **Backed by** Entrepreneur First, Transpose Platform, Boundless Ventures, and NPU Ventures.

## Developer API: Invariant Earth API

A REST API for US coordinates. Request specific fields through `POST /v1/fetch`. The catalog describes datasets for parcel matches, terrain, hazards, and infrastructure. The response contract includes field-level status, source URL, dataset vintage, fetch time, and confidence. Coverage depends on each field and location.

- [Invariant Earth API docs](https://docs.invariant-ai.com/): introduction, quickstart, API reference.
- [Docs index for LLMs](https://docs.invariant-ai.com/llms.txt) and [full docs as Markdown](https://docs.invariant-ai.com/llms-full.txt).
- [Use with AI agents](https://docs.invariant-ai.com/agents): tool definitions for Claude and OpenAI.
- [Public field catalog](https://api.invariant-ai.com/v1/meta/fields) and [field response format](https://docs.invariant-ai.com/responses).

## Data center site due diligence and power studies

Invariant runs due diligence on US data center sites in two steps, for developers, investors, lenders, landowners and brokers (including white-label work for advisers).

- **Step 1, site feasibility screen (within 24 hours):** from a coordinate or parcel and a target MW: serving utility and ISO, nearest substations and lines with a screening MW range for the next three study years and the binding constraint, FEMA flood zone, USGS and ASCE 7 seismic values, wetlands, listed species, FAA Part 77 airspace, zoning and data center moratoriums, water, fiber, gas and parcel. Ends in a go, no-go or conditional go.
- **Step 2, utility-grade power study (usually within 48 hours):** the transmission network around the site rebuilt per study year and checked against ISO-reported flows; AC power flow at N-0 and N-1 (NERC TPL-001 P1, plus selected P2, P4, P5, P7 events) at every connection option, including new switching stations; thermal and voltage limits, short circuit ratio, upgrade search with MW unlocked, indicative cost ranges and an energization date range; utility tariff, fees and pre-application questions.
- **Relation to the utility:** figures are screening figures built to utility planning methods. The utility's own load study, filed with site control, is what makes a number firm.
- **Pricing:** fixed fee per site, quoted before work starts, with portfolio rates; a small fraction of a utility study fee ($10,000 to $100,000 at AEP Ohio, $100,000 for large loads in ERCOT).
- **Request a screen:** email pranav@invariant-ai.com or call (628) 220-8972 with the coordinate, MW and energize-by date, or book at https://cal.com/pranav-goswami/website-30min.

- [Data center site due diligence: feasibility screen first, then a utility-grade power study](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-site-due-diligence): How data center site due diligence works in two steps: a feasibility screen (power, flood, seismic, wetlands, FAA, zoning) and a utility-grade power study with N-1 tests.
- [Data center site feasibility study: power, flood, seismic and zoning screen in 24 hours](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-site-feasibility-study): A data center site feasibility study from Invariant: power at nearby substations, flood zone, seismic, wetlands, FAA, zoning and parcel checks, with a go or no-go in 24 hours.
- [Utility-grade power study for data centers: N-1 power flow before you file with the utility](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/utility-grade-power-study): A utility-grade power study for a data center site: AC power flow and N-1 contingency tests at each connection point, MW by year, upgrades, indicative cost and energization date.
- [Power flow study for a data center: what it tests and how to read the results](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-power-flow-study): What a power flow (load flow) study is for a data center interconnection, what it tests, what inputs it needs, and how to read the MW, the binding element and the upgrades.
- [How N-1 contingency analysis tests a data center’s power headroom](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/n-1-contingency-analysis-data-center): A worked 60 MW example shows how a connection can pass with both lines in service and exceed its thermal limit after a single outage.
- [How to check if a substation has capacity for a data center](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-substation-capacity-check): How to check substation capacity for a data center: what you can learn from records, why hosting capacity maps miss large loads, and when you need a power flow study.
- [How much does a utility load study cost for a data center, and how long does it take?](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/utility-load-study-cost-and-timeline): Utility load study cost and timeline for data centers in 2026: AEP Ohio, ERCOT and Dominion fees, security, study clocks, and how to avoid paying for the wrong study.
- [Distance to substation and transmission for a data center site: what it costs and what it doesn’t tell you](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/distance-to-transmission-line-data-center): How distance to a substation or transmission line affects a data center site: cost per mile by voltage, switching station costs, right-of-way time, and why distance is not capacity.
- [Data center flood zone screening: FEMA zones, base flood elevation and what to check](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-flood-zone-screening): How to screen a data center site for flood risk: FEMA flood zones (A, AE, V, X), the National Flood Hazard Layer, access roads, substations and sea level exposure.
- [Data center seismic risk screening: USGS hazard maps, ASCE 7 values and faults](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-seismic-risk-screening): How to screen a data center site for seismic risk: the USGS National Seismic Hazard Model, ASCE 7 seismic design category, site soils and mapped faults.
- [Data center environmental screening: wetlands, endangered species and Phase I ESA](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-environmental-site-screening): How to screen a data center site for wetlands, listed species and contamination before you buy: National Wetlands Inventory, IPaC, EPA cleanup records and the Phase I ESA.
- [FAA height limits near airports: what a data center site needs to check](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/faa-height-limits-data-center-site): FAA Part 77 for data center sites: when notice is required for buildings, stacks and cranes near airports, the 200 ft and 100:1 tests, and how to check a site.
- [Power due diligence for data center investors and lenders: what to ask before you underwrite](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-power-due-diligence-investors): Data center power due diligence for investors and lenders: which utility documents count, what a power study should show, and the red flags in a powered land deal.
- [Selling land to a data center developer? Get a power study first](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/power-study-before-selling-land-to-data-center): For landowners and brokers: why a power study changes what data center developers pay for land, what it should show, and how to get one before you market the site.

## Data center capacity for neoclouds and AI labs

Invariant finds US data center capacity for GPU clusters (colocation that can cool dense racks, built and energized sites, powered land) sized from GPU count, rack density and date, and checks the power behind each option against utility documents. It also runs an independent power check on a provider or site before an AI tenant signs: the document behind the MW, the point of interconnection, upgrades, competing loads and on-site generation permits, usually within 48 hours.

- **Sizing rule used on our pages:** NVIDIA system power (DGX H100 10.2 kW and DGX B200 14.3 kW per 8 GPUs; GB200 NVL72 about 120 kW per 72-GPU rack), plus about 10% for networking and storage, times PUE 1.3. About 1.8 kW (H100), 2.6 kW (B200) and 2.4 kW (GB200) per GPU at the meter.
- **Request capacity:** email pranav@invariant-ai.com or call (628) 220-8972 with GPU type and count, rack density, date and regions.

- [Data center capacity for neoclouds and AI labs: power, space and cooling for your GPUs (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/ai-compute-capacity-for-neoclouds): Where neoclouds and smaller AI labs find data center capacity in 2026: MW per GPU count, colocation vs powered shell vs land, liquid cooling, and how to check a power date.
- [How much power does a GPU cluster need? H100, B200 and GB200 NVL72 in MW](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/gpu-cluster-power-requirements): GPU cluster power requirements in MW: H100, B200 and GB200 NVL72 from 256 to 100,000 GPUs, kW per GPU, rack density, PUE and what to ask a data center for.
- [GPU colocation for AI labs and neoclouds: what to ask a provider before you sign](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/gpu-colocation-for-ai-labs): GPU colocation checklist for AI labs and neoclouds: power per cabinet, liquid cooling, energized vs contracted MW, delivery dates, minimum terms, fiber and SLAs.
- [Liquid cooling for GPU racks: what a data center needs for 40 to 130 kW racks](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/liquid-cooling-gpu-data-center): What a data center needs for liquid-cooled GPU racks: rear-door heat exchangers, direct-to-chip, CDUs, facility water, and how to tell a liquid-ready hall from a real one.
- [Where a small AI lab can put 1 to 10 MW of GPUs in the US](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/small-gpu-cluster-1-to-10-mw): Options for a small AI lab or neocloud needing 1 to 10 MW for GPUs: colocation, Tier III rooms, energized edge and mining sites, with timing and what to check.
- [Build, lease or colocate: how neoclouds and AI labs get to power fastest](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/neocloud-build-lease-or-colocate): Build vs lease vs colocate for neoclouds and AI labs: time to power, capital, control and risk at 5, 50 and 500 MW, and when to move from one to the next.
- [Power longstop dates in GPU and data center leases: check the provider’s power before you sign](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/gpu-lease-power-longstop-diligence): How AI tenants and neoclouds protect a GPU deployment date: power longstop clauses, what document backs a provider’s MW, and the power check to run before signing.
- [Power check on a data center provider or site for AI tenants and neoclouds](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/provider-power-check-for-ai-tenants): An independent power check for AI tenants and neoclouds: the document behind a provider’s MW, the connection, competing loads, upgrades and a realistic power date, in 48 hours.

## Data centres in India

Guides to data centre locations, state and national policy, approvals, power and grid connection, open access charges, land, water, and physical risks in India.
- [Data centre approvals in India](https://invariant-ai.com/data-centre-compliance-india): authorities and primary sources for project approvals.
- [Data centres in India: capacity, cities, companies, policy and power (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centres-in-india.md): India had about 1.6 to 1.8 GW of live data centre capacity in mid-2026, half of it in Mumbai. Data centre counts by city, the operators, policy and power supply.
- [How to find a data centre site in India: power, fibre, land and risk (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/find-data-centre-site-india.md): Finding a data centre site in India starts with written power evidence. Compare Mumbai (890 MW, 7.9% vacancy in H1 2026), Chennai, Hyderabad and others on risk.
- [Approvals needed for a data centre in India: permits, NOCs and who issues them](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centre-approvals-india.md): Approvals for a data centre in India: no single licence, but EC at 20,000 sq m or more, CTE and CTO, groundwater, airport height and fire NOCs, diesel licence.
- [How to set up a data centre in India: from entity to energisation (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/how-to-set-up-data-centre-india.md): How to set up a data centre in India in nine steps: size the load, form the entity, pick a state, confirm power before land, get approvals, inspect and energise.
- [Data centre cost per MW in India: ₹35 to 75 crore to build, plus land (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centre-cost-per-mw-india.md): Data centre cost per MW in India: ₹35 to 75 crore to build on SBI’s April 2026 figures, US$7.4 million on Cushman & Wakefield’s. Land, rents and financing.
- [Data centre site due diligence in India: the feasibility checklist (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centre-site-due-diligence-india.md): Data centre site due diligence in India: power evidence, title, groundwater (730 of 6,762 units over-exploited), seismic zone, flood history and AAI height limits.
- [Data centre land in India: acres per MW, land prices and powered land (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centre-land-india.md): Data centre land in India costs ₹3 to 60 crore per acre and about half an acre per MW on Anarock’s 2026 bands. Recent deals, parks, FAR rules and powered land.
- [Seismic zones, flood and cyclone risk for data centres in India (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centre-seismic-flood-risk-india.md): Seismic zones of Indian data centre cities under IS 1893 (Delhi IV; Mumbai and Chennai III), the withdrawn Zone VI map, record floods, cyclones and CRZ limits.
- [Water for data centres in India: groundwater NOC, water stress and state rules](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centre-water-india.md): Data centres in India need a CGWA or state NOC to draw groundwater. Anarock puts use at about 25.5 million litres per MW a year. Water-stressed cities, state rules.
- [Power for data centres in India: grid supply, open access and tariffs by state](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/power-for-data-centres-india.md): How data centres in India buy power: discom supply, green open access from 100 kW, captive plants, and state tariffs such as Tamil Nadu’s ₹7.50/kWh plus ₹608/kVA.
- [Data centre grid connection in India: voltage by load, dual grid and GNA (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-centre-grid-connection-india.md): Data centre grid connection in India: supply moves to 110, 132 or 220 kV above about 10 MVA, who pays for lines and bays, and direct inter-state access from 50 MW.
- [Green energy open access for data centres in India: rules, banking and ISTS (2026)](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/green-energy-open-access-data-centres-india.md): Green energy open access for data centres in India: 100 kW eligibility, 15-day deemed approval, monthly banking, the ISTS waiver phase-out to 2028 and captive rules.

- [Data center acres per MW: land sizing for AI campuses, colocation and mining](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-land-acres-per-mw): How many acres a data center needs per MW: PUE, rack density, substation and cooling footprints, real campus examples and a quick check of listing acreage against MW.
- [Data center moratoriums: how to screen a county before you option land](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-moratorium-local-opposition-site-screening): How to check a US county for data center moratoriums, rezoning fights and new ordinances before optioning land, with 2025 to 2026 cases and a practical kill sheet.
- [Data center site selection: the US permitting work to do before committing](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-site-selection-permitting): A US due diligence guide to data center siting, zoning, utility service, environmental permits, and the evidence to collect before committing to a site.
- [Data center backup generators: how to plan the air-permit path](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-backup-generator-air-permits): A practical US guide to generator-fleet air permitting, emergency-use restrictions, federal engine standards, source aggregation, and operating records.
- [Data center water and stormwater permits](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-water-stormwater-permits): What to verify for data center water supply, sewer discharge, construction dewatering and stormwater. Includes San José permit records and a downloadable checklist.
- [Data center fuel and chemical storage: SPCC and Tier II reporting](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-fuel-storage-spcc-tier-ii): How US data center operators assess diesel and transformer oil under SPCC and prepare EPCRA Tier II inventories for batteries, fuel, and cooling chemicals.
- [Data center refrigerant compliance: Section 608 and AIM Act operating duties](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-refrigerant-compliance): A US guide to data center cooling compliance under Section 608 and the AIM Act, with appliance-level applicability, leak response, automatic detection, and records.
- [Data center UPS and battery permits: settle the fire-code path before procurement](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/data-center-fire-code-battery-requirements): A US guide to data center UPS and battery approvals: NFPA 75 versus NFPA 855, UL 9540 versus UL 9540A, local permits, retrofit reviews, and acceptance evidence.
- [Oil and gas permitting: a U.S. onshore compliance checklist](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/oil-gas-permitting-compliance-checklist): Map federal minerals, state drilling, air, water, and pipeline requirements into a practical permitting sequence for U.S. onshore oil and gas projects.
- [Oil and Gas Methane Compliance: OOOOb and Subpart W Reporting](https://invariant-ai.com/blog/oil-gas-methane-compliance): Check the November 30 OOOOb catch-up deadline and March 10 Subpart W reporting deadline. Compare EPA filings, rule changes and the records operators need.

## Glossary entries (DefinedTerm)

Space:
- [14 CFR Part 413](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/14-cfr-413), FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation regulation in Title 14, Chapter III, Subchapter C that sets the cross-cutting license application procedures for all U.S. commercial launch, reentry, and site licenses.
- [FAA AC 450.41-1](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ac-450-41-1), FAA Advisory Circular 450.41-1 describes the process for submitting and obtaining acceptance of a means of compliance under 14 CFR 450.35 for commercial launch and reentry licensing.
- [ANSI S2.20-1983](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ansi-s2-20), Acoustical Society of America standard for estimating air blast characteristics from single-point explosions, used by FAA AC 450.137-1 as the screening glass damage model for window breakage probability.
- [BIS Commerce Country Chart](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/bis-country-chart), A destination-by-control-reason matrix in Supplement No. 1 to 15 CFR Part 738 that exporters cross-reference against an ECCN to determine whether an EAR license is required.
- [COMSTAC](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/comstac), The Commercial Space Transportation Advisory Committee is a FACA-chartered federal advisory body that advises the Secretary of Transportation, through the FAA, on commercial space transportation policy and regulation.
- [ECCN 9A521](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ec-cn-9a521), A common but inexact shorthand for the Commerce Control List entries covering specially designed spacecraft components transferred from the USML, properly classified at ECCN 9A515.x under 15 CFR Part 774.
- [ECSS](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ecss), ECSS is the European Cooperation for Space Standardization, a coherent single set of standards for space project management, engineering, and product assurance maintained by ESA, industry, and national agencies.
- [ECSS-E-ST-10-03](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ecss-e-st-10-03), ECSS-E-ST-10-03C Rev.1 (31 May 2022) is the European space engineering standard defining ground verification testing requirements for spacecraft segment elements and equipment before launch.
- [Executive Order 14335](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/eo-14335), EO 14335, "Enabling Competition in the Commercial Space Industry", signed August 2025, directed the Department of Transportation to reevaluate, amend, or rescind portions of 14 CFR Part 450 within 120 days and referenced AI in commercial space safety research.
- [FAA AST](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-ast), The FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation, the U.S. agency that licenses commercial launch and reentry under 51 USC Chapter 509 and 14 CFR Parts 400 to 460.
- [FAA Categorical Exclusion](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-categorical-exclusion), A NEPA determination under FAA Order 1050.1F that a proposed action, including a 14 CFR Part 450 launch or reentry license, normally has no significant environmental effect and needs no EA or EIS.
- [FAA Part 450](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-part-450), FAA Part 450 is the performance-based 14 CFR rule that consolidates commercial launch and reentry licensing into a single, vehicle-agnostic framework, effective March 10, 2021.
- [FCC 22-74 (5-year deorbit)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fcc-22-74), FCC 22-74 is the Second Report and Order adopted September 29, 2022 that shortened the post-mission disposal benchmark for LEO satellites from 25 years to 5 years.
- [FCC market access](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fcc-market-access), The FCC process under 47 CFR 25.137 by which a non-U.S. licensed satellite system obtains authority to provide service to or from earth stations located in the United States.
- [FCC Part 25](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fcc-part-25), 47 CFR Part 25 is the FCC rule set that licenses commercial satellite communications, covering U.S. space stations, earth stations, and non-U.S. market access requests.
- [FCC Part 5](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fcc-part-5), 47 CFR Part 5 is the FCC's Experimental Radio Service rule, which authorizes non-commercial experimentation, product development, and market trials, including space and earth station experimental authorizations.
- [FCC Part 97](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fcc-part-97), FCC 47 CFR Part 97 governs the U.S. Amateur Radio Service, including amateur satellites operated under noncommercial rules, with space station requirements set in Section 97.207.
- [FCC Schedule S](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fcc-schedule-s), FCC Form 312 Schedule S is the structured satellite engineering data form required for Part 25 space station applications, capturing beam, frequency, EIRP, G/T, and orbit parameters.
- [Flight Safety System (FSS)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/flight-safety-system), The high-reliability onboard plus ground system, required under 14 CFR 450.145, that terminates or aborts a launch or reentry vehicle whose failure would endanger the public.
- [GIMS GXT file format](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/gxt-format), ITU-defined textual file format that encodes satellite antenna gain contour diagrams, used in FCC Schedule S exhibit S8 to satisfy 47 CFR 25.114 antenna pattern submission requirements.
- [IADC Space Debris Mitigation Guidelines](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/iadc), The international consensus framework (IADC-02-01) for limiting orbital debris, structured around protected LEO and GEO regions, post-mission disposal, and on-orbit passivation across all spaceflight phases.
- [IADC and UN COPUOS debris guidelines](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/imo-debris), Voluntary international space debris mitigation guidelines, drafted by IADC in 2002 and adopted by UN COPUOS in 2007, codifying disposal practice for LEO and GEO operators.
- [IN-SPACe NGP 2024](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/in-space-ngp-2024), IN-SPACe NGP 2024 is the May 2024 norms document operationalising the Indian Space Policy 2023 by setting authorisation procedures for six categories of space activities by Indian entities.
- [ISO 24113](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/iso-24113), ISO 24113:2023 is the top-level international standard defining space debris mitigation requirements for unmanned spacecraft and launch vehicle orbital stages operating in or transiting near-Earth space.
- [ITU API and CR/C filings](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/itu-api-crc), ITU Radio Regulations procedure under Articles 9 and 11 in which an operator files Advance Publication Information then a Coordination Request, securing a frequency assignment within a 7-year deadline.
- [Kessler syndrome](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/kessler-syndrome), A self-sustaining collisional cascade in low Earth orbit in which fragment-generating impacts raise debris density until further collisions become inevitable, rendering affected orbital regimes unusable.
- [Liability Convention 1972](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/liability-convention), The 1972 UN treaty establishing absolute liability of launching states for surface and aircraft damage caused by space objects, and fault-based liability for damage in space.
- [License Exception CSA](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/license-exception-csa), License Exception Commercial Space Activities (CSA) is a Bureau of Industry and Security authorization, proposed in October 2024, allowing license-free exports of specified space items to close allies and U.S. persons.
- [MIL-STD-461](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/mil-std-461), MIL-STD-461 is the U.S. Department of Defense interface standard governing electromagnetic interference emission and susceptibility characteristics of electronic subsystems and equipment.
- [NASA GEVS](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nasa-gevs), NASA Goddard's General Environmental Verification Standard (GSFC-STD-7000), the agency baseline that defines test levels and methods for qualifying spacecraft hardware to mission environments.
- [NOAA Commercial Remote Sensing Licensing](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/noaa-csla), A NOAA licensing regime under 15 CFR Part 960 that authorizes private Earth remote sensing space systems and sorts them into three tiers based on data availability.
- [NOAA Tiers 1, 2, 3](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/noaa-tier-1-2-3), A three-tier U.S. commercial remote-sensing licensing framework under 15 CFR Part 960 (effective July 20, 2020) that scales license conditions based on whether comparable unenhanced data is available from foreign or domestic sources.
- [U.S. Government ODMSP](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/odmsp), The U.S. Government Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices, first issued in 2001 and revised November 2019, set the baseline debris rules for NASA, FCC, NOAA, and FAA licensees.
- [ITU Resolution 49 (Rev. WRC-19)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/resolution-49), ITU procedure requiring an administration to file identity data on the satellite network operator, spacecraft manufacturer, and launch services provider within the seven-year bringing-into-use period.
- [FAA SLR-2](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/slr-2), FAA rulemaking effort to revise 14 CFR Part 450, launched in response to the August 2025 SpARC final report and Executive Order 14335 of August 13, 2025.
- [Commercial Space Launch Amendments Act of 2024](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/space-launch-safety-act), Informal label for the 2024 statutory amendments to U.S. commercial space launch law, enacted across P.L. 118-63 and P.L. 118-159, that reset FAA AST authorities and extended the human-spaceflight learning period.
- [FAA Spaceport License](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/spaceport-license), An FAA Launch Site Operator License issued under 14 CFR Part 420 that authorizes a commercial spaceport operator to offer a launch site to multiple launch and reentry vehicle operators.
- [Thermal vacuum (TVAC)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/thermal-vacuum-tvac), Thermal vacuum (TVAC) is an environmental test that exposes spacecraft hardware to high vacuum and cyclic hot and cold extremes to verify thermal design, workmanship, and functional performance.
- [UN Outer Space Treaty](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/unoosa-ost), The 1967 multilateral treaty governing State activity in outer space, establishing non-appropriation, State responsibility for national activities, launching-State liability, and a duty to avoid harmful contamination.
- [USML Category IV](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/usml-cat-iv), USML Category IV controls launch vehicles, guided and ballistic missiles, rockets, torpedoes, bombs, mines, and their specially designed parts under U.S. State Department ITAR jurisdiction.
- [USML Category XV](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/usml-category-xv), USML Category XV is the ITAR control list at 22 CFR 121.1 covering spacecraft and related articles whose export is licensed by the State Department's DDTC.

Nuclear:
- [10 CFR Part 100](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/10-cfr-part-100), U.S. NRC regulation establishing reactor site suitability criteria, including exclusion area, low population zone, population center distance, and geologic and seismic siting requirements for power and testing reactors.
- [10 CFR Part 110](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/10-cfr-part-110), Nuclear Regulatory Commission regulation governing export and import of nuclear equipment, material, and related technology, prescribing general and specific license procedures under the Atomic Energy Act.
- [10 CFR Part 50](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/10-cfr-part-50), 10 CFR Part 50 is the NRC's legacy two-step reactor licensing rule, issuing a construction permit and then a separate operating license for production and utilization facilities.
- [10 CFR Part 52](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/10-cfr-part-52), The U.S. NRC regulation, codified in 1989, that authorises a one-step Combined Licence for nuclear power plants alongside Early Site Permits and Standard Design Certifications.
- [10 CFR Part 53](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/10-cfr-part-53), 10 CFR Part 53 is the NRC's risk-informed, technology-inclusive, performance-based licensing framework for commercial nuclear plants, offered as an optional alternative to Parts 50 and 52.
- [10 CFR Part 71](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/10-cfr-part-71), U.S. NRC regulation governing packaging and transportation of radioactive material, setting Type A and Type B package design, testing, and quality assurance standards for licensed shipments.
- [10 CFR Part 73](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/10-cfr-part-73), NRC regulation titled "Physical Protection of Plants and Materials" that establishes security requirements for nuclear facilities, special nuclear material, and the Design Basis Threat licensees must defend against.
- [Section 123 Agreement](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/123-agreement), A bilateral peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement concluded under Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, required before the United States may license significant exports of nuclear material, equipment, or sensitive technology.
- [Atomic Energy Act of 1954](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/aea-1954), The foundational US statute (P.L. 83-703, 42 USC 2011 et seq.) that opened nuclear technology to private industry and established the federal civilian licensing framework.
- [Atomic Energy Regulatory Board](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/aerb), The AERB is the Indian nuclear and radiation safety regulator, given statutory standing under the SHANTI Act 2025 with powers of licensing, inspection, suspension, and penalty over all civilian nuclear and radiation facilities in India.
- [ALARA](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/alara), "As low as is reasonably achievable," the NRC radiation protection principle in 10 CFR 20.1003 requiring licensees to drive doses below regulatory limits using practical, economically justified measures.
- [ARCAP](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/arcap), ARCAP is the U.S. NRC project that produced technology-inclusive, risk-informed guidance covering the non-safety-analysis content of advanced reactor applications under 10 CFR Parts 50, 52, and 53.
- [ARDP](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ardp), U.S. Department of Energy program launched in 2020 to cost-share two full-scale advanced reactor demonstrations, TerraPower's Natrium and X-energy's Xe-100, within seven years.
- [ASHVINI (Anushakti Vidhyut Nigam)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ashvini), ASHVINI, formally Anushakti Vidhyut Nigam Limited, is a 51 percent NPCIL and 49 percent NTPC joint venture approved on 11 September 2024 and restructured on 9 January 2025 with authorised share capital of Rs 15,000 crore, set up to build large new-build nuclear capacity in India.
- [ASME/ANS RA-S](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/asme-ans-ra-s), Joint ASME and ANS family of consensus PRA standards establishing technical requirements for Level 1 and Level 2 probabilistic risk assessments at U.S. commercial nuclear power plants.
- [ASME Section III](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/asme-section-iii), ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section III sets construction rules for nuclear facility components, classifying them as Class 1, 2, or 3 by safety significance.
- [ASNR (France)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/asnr), France's independent civil nuclear regulator, the Autorité de sûreté nucléaire et de radioprotection, formed on 1 January 2025 by merging ASN and IRSN.
- [Atomic Canyon](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/atomic-canyon), Atomic Canyon is a US AI-for-nuclear-compliance company that ships Neutron, an ADAMS-indexed search product backed by the open-source FERMI sentence-embedding model family trained on the Oak Ridge Frontier supercomputer.
- [Bharat Small Reactor](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/bharat-small-reactor), The Bharat Small Reactor (BSR) program is NPCIL's 220 MWe pressurised heavy water reactor offered to private industrial users under a captive use commercial model, financed by the industrial partner and operated by NPCIL under AERB licence.
- [Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/clnda), The CLNDA was the Indian statute that defined nuclear operator liability and the controversial right of recourse against suppliers under Section 17(b). It was repealed on 20 December 2025 by the SHANTI Act.
- [IAEA Convention on Nuclear Safety](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/cns), A 1994 international treaty, administered by the IAEA and in force since 1996, that commits Contracting Parties to safety obligations for land-based civil nuclear power plants enforced through three-yearly peer review.
- [CNSC (Canada)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/cnsc), Canada's independent federal nuclear regulator, established May 31, 2000 under the Nuclear Safety and Control Act, overseeing reactors, the fuel cycle, uranium mining, and nuclear substances.
- [Combined License (COL)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/combined-license), A Combined License issued under 10 CFR 52 Subpart C is a single NRC authorization to both construct and operate a nuclear power facility, contingent on satisfying ITAAC.
- [Convention on Supplementary Compensation for Nuclear Damage](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/csc-nuclear-damage), The Convention on Supplementary Compensation for Nuclear Damage (CSC) is the IAEA-administered umbrella treaty that creates a global supplementary fund for nuclear damages and aligns operator liability ceilings at 300 million SDR.
- [Department of Atomic Energy](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/dae), The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) is the Government of India department, established 1954, that administers civilian atomic energy policy, the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, NPCIL, and other reserved-activity research institutions.
- [NRC DANU](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/danu), DANU is the NRC Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation division that since 2022 has led pre-application engagement and licensing review for advanced reactors and non-power facilities.
- [Early Site Permit (ESP)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/early-site-permit), A U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission approval under 10 CFR 52 Subpart A that resolves site safety, environmental, and emergency planning issues for one or more future nuclear power reactors, independent of design.
- [Executive Order 14301](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/eo-14301), EO 14301, "Reforming Nuclear Reactor Testing at the Department of Energy", signed 23 May 2025, established the DOE Advanced Reactor Pilot Program to authorise at least three privately funded test reactors to reach criticality by 4 July 2026 outside the national laboratories.
- [NRC Emergency Planning Zone](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/epz), Geographic area around a U.S. commercial nuclear reactor for which detailed offsite emergency planning is required under 10 CFR 50.47, sized to accident consequences.
- [Energy Reorganization Act of 1974](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/era-1974), Federal statute (Pub. L. 93-438, 88 Stat. 1233) that abolished the Atomic Energy Commission and split its functions between a new Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Energy Research and Development Administration.
- [Everstar Gordian](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/everstar), Everstar is a New York-based AI-for-nuclear-compliance startup whose Gordian product is a retrieval-augmented platform with deterministic compute paths for numerical claims, used in the NRIC HTGR demonstration with Idaho National Laboratory and Microsoft.
- [FermiBench](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fermi-bench), FermiBench is the Invariant-published benchmark for retrieval over the NRC ADAMS regulatory corpus, with the public ADAMS search interface as the comparison probe. The Helion-512 model scores 0.9693 nDCG at 10.
- [Helion-512](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/helion-512), Helion-512 is the Invariant retrieval model that scores 0.9693 nDCG at 10 on FermiBench, the published state of the art on retrieval over the NRC regulatory corpus.
- [IAEA Nuclear Activities Authorisation](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/iaea-naa), Composite IAEA framework under which States authorise peaceful nuclear activities, combining INFCIRC/153 safeguards obligations with GSR Part 1 (Rev. 1) regulatory authorisation requirements for facilities and activities.
- [IAEA SF-1](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/iaea-sf-1), IAEA Safety Standards Series No. SF-1 (2006), the Safety Fundamentals document that states the fundamental safety objective and ten principles underpinning all subsequent IAEA nuclear and radiation safety requirements.
- [IAEA SSR-2/1](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/iaea-ssr-2-1), IAEA Specific Safety Requirements No. SSR-2/1 establishes design requirements for civilian land-based stationary nuclear power plants, currently in Revision 1 published in 2016.
- [Inductive (Nuclear Licensing Accelerator)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/inductive), Inductive, operating as Nuclear Licensing Accelerator and headquartered in San Francisco, is an AI-for-nuclear-compliance startup that markets itself as "TurboTax for nuclear licensing" with a collaborative authoring workspace built on the OpenPRA schema.
- [IAEA INFCIRC/153](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/infcirc-153), IAEA INFCIRC/153 (Corrected), issued June 1972, is the model Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement that every non-nuclear-weapon State party to the NPT must conclude under Article III.
- [NRC Inspection Manual](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/inspection-manual), The NRC's public compilation of Inspection Manual Chapters (IMCs) and Inspection Procedures (IPs) that govern how staff inspect, document, and assess licensee activities.
- [ITAAC Post-Closure Notification](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ipcn), A licensee filing under 10 CFR 52.99(c)(2) reporting new information that materially alters the basis for a previously submitted ITAAC closure, made before the 52.103(g) finding.
- [ITAAC](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/itaac), ITAAC are the inspections, tests, analyses, and acceptance criteria written into a 10 CFR Part 52 combined license that the NRC must find complete before fuel load.
- [Kairos Hermes](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/kairos-hermes), Kairos Power's 35 MWt fluoride-salt-cooled high-temperature test reactor at Oak Ridge, the first non-light-water construction permit issued by the NRC in over 50 years.
- [KBS-3](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/kbs-3), KBS-3 is the Swedish multi-barrier concept for final disposal of spent nuclear fuel in copper canisters within bentonite clay roughly 500 metres deep in crystalline bedrock.
- [NRC LIC-111](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/lic-111), NRC NRR Office Instruction LIC-111, Revision 2 (issued December 30, 2024, ML24309A281), the staff guidance governing planning, conduct, and reporting of regulatory audits.
- [NRC LIC-115](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/lic-115), NRR Office Instruction governing how NRC staff prepare, clarify, and issue Requests for Additional Information to applicants, with a 30-day default response window and tiered acceptance versus detailed review RAI tracks.
- [NRC LIC-117](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/lic-117), NRC Office Instruction governing the acceptance review of new reactor license applications, verifying completeness and technical sufficiency before docketing for detailed technical review.
- [LIC-500](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/lic-500), LIC-500 is the U.S. NRC Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation office instruction governing the topical report process, most recently issued as Revision 9 in January 2022.
- [NEI 18-04](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nei-18-04), Nuclear Energy Institute guidance, Revision 1 (August 2019), defining the Licensing Modernization Project methodology for non-light-water reactor licensing basis development, endorsed by NRC Regulatory Guide 1.233.
- [NEI 21-04](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nei-21-04), Nuclear Energy Institute industry guidance, issued in 2021, prescribing a standardized format and best practices for applicant responses to NRC Requests for Additional Information (RAIs).
- [NEI 21-07 (TICAP)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nei-21-07-ticap), NEI 21-07 Revision 1 is the Technology Inclusive Content of Application Project guideline, endorsed by NRC Regulatory Guide 1.253 in April 2024, defining a risk-informed, performance-based safety analysis report format for non-LWR license applications.
- [NEIMA](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/neima), NEIMA is the Nuclear Energy Innovation and Modernization Act, Public Law 115-439 (January 14, 2019), directing the NRC to build a technology-inclusive regulatory framework and reform fee recovery for advanced reactors.
- [NEPA review](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nepa), NRC environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, producing an Environmental Impact Statement that informs nuclear reactor licensing decisions under 10 CFR Part 51.
- [NEPA Environmental Assessment](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nepa-ea), A concise NEPA screening document, capped at 75 pages and a one-year deadline, that determines whether a federal action requires a full Environmental Impact Statement or a Finding of No Significant Impact.
- [Nuclear Power Corporation of India](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/npcil), NPCIL is the Government of India undertaking under the Department of Atomic Energy that designs, builds, owns, and operates India's civilian nuclear power plants, including under the Bharat Small Reactor program and the ASHVINI joint venture.
- [Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/npt), The 1968 multilateral treaty, in force since 5 March 1970, that binds 191 states to three pillars: non-proliferation, peaceful nuclear cooperation, and pursuit of nuclear disarmament.
- [NRA (Japan)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nra-japan), Japan's Nuclear Regulation Authority, the independent civilian regulator established 19 September 2012 under the Ministry of the Environment to oversee all civil nuclear safety and security.
- [NRC Certificate of Compliance](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nrc-coc), An NRC-issued approval listing a specific dry spent fuel storage cask design at 10 CFR 72.214, authorizing power reactor licensees to load it under a Part 72 general license.
- [NRC SECY paper](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nrc-secy), A SECY paper is a written issue paper that NRC staff submit through the Office of the Secretary to the five Commissioners, recommending a policy, rulemaking, licensing, or adjudicatory decision.
- [SECY-23-0021](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nrc-secy-23-0021), NRC staff paper dated March 1, 2023, transmitting the draft proposed 10 CFR Part 53 rule, a risk-informed, technology-inclusive licensing framework for commercial nuclear plants.
- [10 CFR 2.815 (acceptance review)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nrcpr), NRC regulation governing docketing and acceptance review of standard design certification applications, requiring a completeness and technical adequacy determination generally within 30 days of tender.
- [NUREG-0800 (SRP)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nureg-0800), NRC Standard Review Plan, LWR Edition: chapter-by-chapter guidance that NRC staff use to review safety analysis reports for nuclear power plant licensing.
- [NuScale VOYGR](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/nuscale-voygr), NuScale's small modular reactor plant family, built from 77 MWe NuScale Power Modules; the original 50 MWe variant was certified by the NRC in 2023 under 10 CFR Part 52 Appendix G.
- [Oklo Aurora](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/oklo-aurora), A 1.5 MWe sodium-cooled fast microreactor whose custom combined license application became the first advanced-reactor COLA denied without prejudice by the NRC on January 6, 2022.
- [ONR Generic Design Assessment](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/onr-gda), A voluntary four-step UK regulatory review by the Office for Nuclear Regulation and Environment Agency that assesses a new reactor design generically before any site-specific licensing.
- [10 CFR Part 810](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/part-810), 10 CFR Part 810 is the US Department of Energy regulation governing transfer of unclassified nuclear technology to foreign nationals or facilities, administered through general and specific authorisations under DOE's Atomic Energy Act Section 57b.(2) authority.
- [PSAR / FSAR](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/psar-fsar), The PSAR and FSAR are the two-stage Safety Analysis Reports an applicant submits to the U.S. NRC under 10 CFR 50.34 to obtain a construction permit and operating license.
- [RAI (Request for Additional Information)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rai-nrc), A Request for Additional Information is the formal NRC docket mechanism by which staff ask a license applicant to supply or clarify information needed to complete a regulatory finding.
- [NRC RG 1.183](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-1-183), U.S. NRC Regulatory Guide issued July 2000 establishing the alternative source term (AST) methodology and assumptions for analyzing design basis accident radiological consequences at light-water reactors.
- [NRC RG 1.200](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-1-200), U.S. NRC Regulatory Guide 1.200 endorses, with conditions, the ASME/ANS PRA Standard as an acceptable approach for risk-informed licensing activities at commercial nuclear plants.
- [Regulatory Guide 1.206](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-1-206), Regulatory Guide 1.206 Revision 1 (October 2018) is the NRC's consolidated guidance on the format and content of 10 CFR Part 52 applications for design certifications, early site permits, and combined licenses.
- [Regulatory Guide 1.215](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-1-215), NRC Regulatory Guide 1.215 describes a method the staff finds acceptable for documenting closure of inspections, tests, analyses, and acceptance criteria under 10 CFR Part 52.
- [NRC RG 1.232](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-1-232), NRC Regulatory Guide 1.232 Revision 0, issued April 2018, provides advanced reactor design criteria adapting 10 CFR Part 50 Appendix A GDC for non-light-water reactor principal design criteria.
- [Regulatory Guide 1.233](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-1-233), NRC guidance, issued June 2020 as Revision 0, that endorses NEI 18-04 as one acceptable technology-inclusive, risk-informed, performance-based methodology for non-light-water reactor licensing.
- [NRC RG 1.247](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-1-247), Trial NRC regulatory guide, issued March 2022, that endorses with exceptions ASME/ANS RA-S-1.4-2021 as an acceptable PRA standard for advanced non-light water reactor risk-informed activities.
- [NRC RG 4.7](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rg-4-7), The U.S. NRC Regulatory Guide that defines general site suitability criteria for commercial nuclear power stations, including population density, geology, hydrology, meteorology, and emergency planning factors.
- [SHANTI Act 2025](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/shanti-act), The SHANTI Act is the Indian statute that replaced the Atomic Energy Act 1962 and the CLNDA 2010 with effect from 20 December 2025, opening private reactor build, giving the AERB statutory standing, and replacing the flat operator liability cap with a graded band.
- [NRC Staff Requirements Memorandum](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/srm), A Staff Requirements Memorandum (SRM) is the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission's written direction to staff, recording Commission decisions on a SECY paper plus any tasks and due dates.

Aerospace:
- [FAA AC 25.1309-1](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ac-25-1309), FAA Advisory Circular describing acceptable means of compliance with 14 CFR 25.1309 system safety requirements for transport-category airplanes; current Revision B issued August 30, 2024.
- [FAA AC 25.1309-1B](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ac-25-1309-1b), FAA Advisory Circular providing acceptable means of compliance with 14 CFR 25.1309 for transport aircraft system safety, defining five failure-condition severities and matching probability targets per flight hour.
- [SAE ARP4754A](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/arp-4754a), SAE Aerospace Recommended Practice ARP4754A, dated December 21, 2010, sets the development assurance process for civil aircraft and their systems used in certification.
- [SAE ARP4754B](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/arp-4754b), SAE Aerospace Recommended Practice (Dec 20, 2023) for civil aircraft and systems development, jointly issued as EUROCAE ED-79B, aligned with ARP4761A safety assessment.
- [SAE ARP4761](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/arp-4761), SAE Aerospace Recommended Practice that codifies the safety assessment process for civil airborne systems, defining FHA, PSSA, SSA, and CCA methods to demonstrate compliance with 14 CFR 25.1309.
- [Bilateral Aviation Safety Agreement](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/baa), A government-to-government treaty enabling the FAA and a counterpart civil aviation authority to reciprocally recognize each other's airworthiness approvals, type certificates, and production approvals.
- [Design Assurance Level (DAL A-E)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/dal-a-e), A five-tier civil-aviation rigor scale (A through E) tied to failure-condition severity, dictating how exhaustively airborne systems, hardware, and software must be developed and verified.
- [DO-160](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/do-160), RTCA DO-160G (2010) is the standard defining environmental conditions and test procedures, from temperature and vibration to HIRF and lightning, for certifying airborne electronic equipment.
- [DO-178C](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/do-178c), DO-178C, "Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification," is the 2011 RTCA/EUROCAE standard certification authorities accept as the means of compliance for airborne software.
- [DO-254](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/do-254), DO-254 is the RTCA design assurance standard for airborne electronic hardware, published April 2000 and endorsed by the FAA as an acceptable means of compliance for certification.
- [DO-330](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/do-330), RTCA DO-330 / EUROCAE ED-215, the 2011 Software Tool Qualification Considerations document supplementing DO-178C, defining five Tool Qualification Levels and objectives for qualifying development and verification tools.
- [EASA](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/easa), EASA is the European Union agency responsible for civil aviation safety, established in 2002 to issue type certificates and harmonize airworthiness rules across EU Member States.
- [EASA CS-25](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/easa-cs-25), EASA Certification Specifications CS-25 are the European airworthiness code for turbine-powered large aeroplanes above 5,700 kg MTOW, the structural counterpart to FAA Part 25.
- [eVTOL certification](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/evtol), The regulatory pathway by which electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft earn FAA type, production, and operating approval under the new powered-lift category established in 2024.
- [FAA 14 CFR Part 21](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-part-21), The FAA regulation in Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations that prescribes procedures for certificating civil aircraft, engines, propellers, and articles in the United States.
- [FAA 14 CFR Part 23](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-part-23), FAA airworthiness standards for normal category airplanes up to 19 seats, restructured in 2017 around performance-based rules and industry consensus standards as accepted means of compliance.
- [FAA 14 CFR Part 25](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-part-25), Federal airworthiness standards governing the type certification of transport category airplanes, the design rulebook for jets and large turboprops operated in U.S. civil aviation.
- [FAA 14 CFR Part 27](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-part-27), FAA airworthiness standard governing type certification of normal category rotorcraft with maximum weight of 7,000 pounds or less and nine or fewer passenger seats.
- [FAA 14 CFR Part 29](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-part-29), The FAA airworthiness code for transport category rotorcraft, prescribing type-certification standards for large helicopters above 7,000 lb or with 10 or more passenger seats.
- [FAA 14 CFR Part 33](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/faa-part-33), FAA airworthiness standards governing the type certification of aircraft engines, covering design, construction, and block-test requirements for both reciprocating and turbine powerplants.
- [ICAO](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/icao), ICAO is the United Nations specialized agency that codifies international civil aviation Standards and Recommended Practices through 19 Annexes to the 1944 Chicago Convention.
- [ICAO Annex 14](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/icao-annex-14), ICAO Annex 14 sets the international Standards and Recommended Practices for aerodromes, covering runway geometry, obstacle limitation surfaces, visual aids, and rescue and firefighting services.
- [ICAO Annex 8](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/icao-annex-8), Annex 8 to the Chicago Convention sets Standards and Recommended Practices for the airworthiness of aircraft, defining the minimum design and continuing-airworthiness basis Contracting States must recognize.
- [MIL-STD-810](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/mil-std-810), The U.S. Department of Defense environmental engineering and laboratory test method standard that tailors temperature, vibration, shock, humidity, and altitude testing to a materiel system's life cycle.
- [MIL-STD-882E](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/mil-std-882e), U.S. Department of Defense Standard Practice for System Safety, issued 11 May 2012, defining the systems-engineering approach for identifying hazards and managing risk across defense systems.
- [Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/mosa), MOSA is the US DoD statutory acquisition strategy, codified at 10 USC 4401, that mandates modular design and consensus-based open interfaces for major defense programs to enable competition and refresh.
- [JARUS SORA](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/sora), A risk-based, ten-step methodology issued by JARUS for authorising uncrewed aircraft operations in the Specific category, calibrating evidence and design assurance to assessed ground and air risk.
- [FAA Special Conditions](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/special-conditions), Design-specific airworthiness regulations the FAA issues under 14 CFR 21.16 when existing standards lack adequate or appropriate safety requirements for a novel or unusual feature.
- [FAA TSO](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/tso), An FAA Technical Standard Order is a minimum performance standard issued for specified articles used on civil aircraft, with authorization granted under 14 CFR Part 21 Subpart O.
- [Type Certificate (TC)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/type-certificate), An FAA design approval issued under 14 CFR 21 Subpart B that certifies an aircraft, engine, or propeller type design meets the applicable airworthiness and environmental requirements.

Data center sites and power:
- [Powered land](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/powered-land), Powered land is a site where electric service for a large load already exists or is documented by the utility: an energized connection, a signed service agreement, a completed load study, or the switchyard of a former power plant.
- [Will-serve letter](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/will-serve-letter), A will-serve letter is a signed utility statement that it intends to provide electric service to a site under its tariff, subject to studies, facilities, agreements and payment. It does not reserve megawatts or fix an energization date.
- [Load study](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/load-study), A load study is a utility engineering review of a specific load at a specific point of service and ramp. It shows whether the system can carry the load, which upgrades are needed and roughly when, and is the first power document a data center buyer can underwrite.
- [Energy service agreement (ESA)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/energy-service-agreement), An energy or electric service agreement is the signed contract under which a utility commits to serve a large load at a point of service on a stated ramp, usually with minimum billing, a contract term and financial security.
- [Large-load tariff](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/large-load-tariff), A large-load tariff is a utility rate schedule written for very large new customers such as data centers, typically adding study fees, collateral, minimum demand charges and long contract terms to protect other customers from stranded costs.
- [Power usage effectiveness (PUE)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/power-usage-effectiveness), PUE is the ratio of total data center facility power to the power delivered to IT equipment. A PUE of 1.3 means a site needs 1.3 MW at the meter for every 1 MW of IT load.
- [Behind-the-meter power](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/behind-the-meter-power), Behind-the-meter power is electricity generated on or next to a data center site and delivered to the load without passing through the utility grid meter, most often from natural gas turbines or reciprocating engines.
- [Texas Senate Bill 6 (SB 6)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/texas-sb-6), Texas Senate Bill 6 (2025) sets interconnection, disclosure and curtailment rules for new or expanded loads of 75 MW or more in ERCOT, implemented through PUCT rules that require a study fee and financial security.
- [ERCOT Batch Zero](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ercot-batch-zero), Batch Zero is ERCOT's 2026 process for studying its large-load interconnection queue as a group rather than one request at a time, classifying hundreds of gigawatts of requested data center and industrial load.
- [Substation withdrawal headroom](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/substation-withdrawal-headroom), Withdrawal headroom is the amount of new load a substation and the transmission behind it can serve without overloading any element under normal and contingency conditions. It, not distance, decides whether land near a substation can be powered.
- [Data center moratorium](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/data-center-moratorium), A data center moratorium is a temporary local or state pause on accepting, approving or permitting new data center projects, usually while a government writes new zoning, water or noise rules.
- [Data center site selection](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/data-center-site-selection), Data center site selection is the process of identifying a location that can support the required power, land, water, fiber, and approvals on a project’s development schedule.
- [Utility-grade power study](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/utility-grade-power-study), A utility-grade power study is a power flow study of a site’s connection options, built to the planning methods utilities use (seasonal cases, study years, AC power flow at N-0 and N-1 under NERC TPL-001), that returns MW by connection point and year, the binding element, upgrades, cost and date.
- [N-1 contingency](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/n-1-contingency), N-1 is the condition with one grid element (a line, transformer or generator) out of service. A new data center load passes N-1 if no element exceeds its emergency rating and no voltage leaves its range after any single outage.
- [Power flow study](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/power-flow-study), A power flow (load flow) study solves the voltages and the flow on every line and transformer in a network for a given pattern of load and generation. For a data center it finds the MW at which the first thermal or voltage limit is crossed at a connection point.
- [Data center site feasibility study](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/data-center-site-feasibility-study), A data center site feasibility study is a first screen of a site from a coordinate and a target MW: power at nearby substations, flood zone, seismic hazard, wetlands and species, airspace, zoning and moratoriums, water, fiber and the parcel, ending in a go or no-go.
- [Point of interconnection](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/point-of-interconnection), The point of interconnection is where a data center’s facilities connect to the utility’s system: a bay at an existing substation, or a new switching station on a passing transmission line. The MW a site can get is studied separately at each one.
- [Neocloud](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/neocloud), A neocloud is a cloud provider built mainly to rent GPU compute for AI training and inference, as distinct from general-purpose hyperscalers. Neoclouds lease, colocate or build data center capacity and sell it on to AI labs and enterprises.
- [GPU colocation](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/gpu-colocation), GPU colocation is renting space, power and cooling in a data center for your own GPU servers. The provider runs the building; you own or lease the hardware. Density, cooling and the delivery date decide whether a hall can take a modern cluster.
- [Rack density](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/rack-density), Rack density is the power drawn by one rack of IT equipment, in kW. GPU clusters run from about 20 kW to about 120 kW per rack, against 5 to 15 kW for typical enterprise racks, and density sets the cooling a data center needs.
- [Power longstop date](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/power-longstop-date), A power longstop date is the date in a data center lease or capacity contract by which firm power must be delivered. If it is missed, the tenant can terminate or receive a set remedy.
- [Open access (electricity, India)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/open-access-india), Open access lets an eligible consumer in India buy electricity from a generator or trader other than its local discom, paying to use the transmission and distribution networks plus surcharges set by the state commission.
- [Green Energy Open Access Rules 2022 (GEOA)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/green-energy-open-access), The Green Energy Open Access Rules 2022 let consumers with 100 kW or more of contracted demand buy renewable power through open access, with approval deemed after 15 days and limits on the surcharges states can charge.
- [Cross subsidy surcharge (CSS)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/cross-subsidy-surcharge), Cross subsidy surcharge is the charge an open access consumer pays its discom to make up the cross subsidy that consumer’s tariff would otherwise have contributed to cheaper tariffs for other consumers.
- [Additional surcharge (open access)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/additional-surcharge), Additional surcharge is a charge on open access consumers, set by the state commission under Section 42(4) of the Electricity Act 2003, to cover the discom’s fixed costs of standing ready to supply them.
- [Wheeling charges](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/wheeling-charges), Wheeling charges are what a consumer or generator pays a discom for carrying electricity over its distribution network, set by the state commission.
- [Group captive power (26% ownership, 51% consumption)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/group-captive), Group captive is an arrangement in which several consumers jointly own a generating plant and qualify as captive users if together they hold at least 26% of its ownership and consume at least 51% of its annual generation; captive users do not pay the cross subsidy surcharge or the additional surcharge.
- [General Network Access (GNA)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/general-network-access), General Network Access is the right, granted under CERC’s 2022 regulations, to inject into or draw from India’s inter-state transmission system. A bulk consumer with 50 MW or more of load can apply to connect to it directly.
- [CTU and STU (central and state transmission utilities)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/ctu-stu), The Central Transmission Utility (CTUIL) plans and coordinates the inter-state transmission system and is the nodal agency for connectivity to it; each state transmission utility (STU) plans and coordinates the state’s intra-state transmission system.
- [Discom (distribution company) and HT/EHV supply](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/discom), A discom is the state distribution licensee that supplies electricity to consumers in its area. A data centre is a discom consumer, and the state supply code sets the voltage it is supplied at from its contract demand.
- [Dual grid supply (two-source supply)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/dual-grid-supply), Dual grid supply is a data centre connection fed from two independent grid sources, so the site keeps power if one fails. Maharashtra’s supply code lets the discom provide multiple sources on request at the consumer’s cost; Uttar Pradesh’s 2026 data centre policy subsidises it for data centre parks.
- [Green tariff (India)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/green-tariff-india), A green tariff is an optional premium a discom customer pays over its normal tariff to have its consumption met from renewable power bought by the discom, without arranging open access itself.
- [Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate (CTE and CTO)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/cte-cto), Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) are the permissions a state pollution control board grants under the Water Act 1974 and the Air Act 1981: CTE before a project is set up, CTO before it starts operating.
- [CPCB pollution category (Red, Orange, Green, White, Blue)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/cpcb-industry-category), The Central Pollution Control Board sorts activities into Red, Orange, Green and White categories by a pollution index score, plus a Blue category for essential environmental services; the category sets consent requirements and inspection frequency.
- [Environmental clearance (EIA Notification 2006)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/environmental-clearance-eia), Environmental clearance is the prior approval required under the EIA Notification 2006 for listed project types. A data centre needs it as a building and construction project of 20,000 sq m or more of built-up area, or as a township or area development project.
- [CGWA groundwater NOC](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/cgwa-noc), A CGWA NOC is the no objection certificate a project needs from the Central Ground Water Authority, or from the state groundwater authority where the state regulates, before it draws groundwater for industrial, infrastructure or mining use.
- [Fire NOC for a data centre](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/fire-noc-data-centre), A fire NOC is the no objection certificate from the fire service confirming a building’s fire and life safety design and installations meet the applicable code; for data centres the base code is the National Building Code 2016, Part 4, occupancy E-3.
- [AAI height NOC (airport height clearance)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/aai-height-noc), An AAI height NOC is the clearance from the Airports Authority of India that a structure’s top elevation will not endanger aircraft, required for sites within 20 km of visual-approach and 56 km of instrument-approach airports.
- [Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 (DPDP Act)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/dpdp-act), The Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 is India’s law on the protection of digital personal data. Its Rules were notified in November 2025 with an 18-month phased compliance timeline.
- [Data localisation (India)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/data-localisation-india), Data localisation is a legal requirement to store or process data within India. The requirements come from sector rules, including those of RBI, SEBI, CERT-In and the telecom Unified Licence, and, for specified data held by significant data fiduciaries, the DPDP Rules 2025.
- [MeitY cloud empanelment and STQC audit](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/meity-empanelment), MeitY empanelment is the Ministry of Electronics and IT’s empanelment of cloud service providers, assessed under an STQC audit scheme. SEBI requires its regulated entities to take cloud services only from MeitY-empanelled providers whose data centres hold a valid STQC audit status.
- [Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure (data centre infrastructure status)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/harmonised-master-list), The Harmonised Master List is the Finance Ministry’s list of infrastructure sub-sectors. Data centres of at least 5 MW IT load were added under Communication on 11 October 2022, giving them infrastructure status.
- [National Data Centre Policy (India)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/national-data-centre-policy), India’s national data centre policy exists only as a draft: MeitY issued one in November 2020 that was never notified, and resumed consultations in August 2025. In October 2026 MediaNama, citing the Indian Express, reported that the draft and timeline of a dedicated policy were not yet public.
- [Essential service status (data centres)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/essential-service-status-data-centre), Essential service status brings data centres under a state’s essential services maintenance law. Uttar Pradesh’s 2026 policy classifies the data centre industry under ESMA as an essential service provider, and Gujarat’s 2026 policy treats data centre operations as an essential service according to a law-firm summary.
- [Data centre park (India)](https://invariant-ai.com/glossary/data-centre-park-india), A data centre park is a category that state data centre policies define for incentives. Uttar Pradesh’s 2026 policy treats a data centre of at least 40 MW of total load as a data centre park.
